hints: Notice that this question asks for two separate tests at once, acidity and chirality, so check each compound for both.
Remember that only a sufficiently strong acid like a carboxylic acid will fizz with Na2CO3, alcohols and esters will not.
For the acids that remain, look for a carbon with four different groups attached, that single chiral centre is the final link.
walkthrough:
**What gives CO2 with carbonate?**

Only acids stronger than carbonic acid will do this. In organic chemistry at this level, that means a carboxylic acid, $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$.

The reaction is:
$$2\text{RCO}_2\text{H} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{RCO}_2\text{Na} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Filter by acidity first**

Compound A has two $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ groups, so it reacts. Compound D has one $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ group, so it reacts.

Compound B has only an alcohol $\text{-OH}$, which is far too weakly acidic. Compound C is an ester, $\text{HCO}_2\text{CH}$, with no acidic proton. So B and C cannot give $\text{CO}_2$.

**Filter by chirality**

A chiral molecule needs a chiral centre, a carbon with four different groups and no plane of symmetry.

Compound A is the cis alkene $\text{HO}_2\text{CCH=CHCO}_2\text{H}$. It is flat around the double bond and has a plane of symmetry, so it is achiral.

Compound D is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(Br)CO}_2\text{H}$. The carbon marked $\text{CH(Br)CO}_2\text{H}$ is bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{Br}$, $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. That is four different groups, so it is chiral and it is the only compound that passes both tests.

options.A: Maleic acid, cis-$\text{HO}_2\text{CCH=CHCO}_2\text{H}$, does contain $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ so it reacts with Na2CO3 to give CO2. However it is achiral because the C=C is planar and the molecule has a plane of symmetry. It fails the chirality test.
options.B: 1-methylcyclohex-2-en-1-ol contains only an alcohol $\text{-OH}$ group. Alcohols are neutral and do not react with Na2CO3, so no CO2 is evolved. Students sometimes confuse any $\text{-OH}$ with an acid, but only $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ and phenols are acidic enough here.
options.C: This is the ester $\text{HCO}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)(CH}_2\text{Br)}$. The central CH is indeed bonded to four different groups, so it is chiral, but esters have no acidic proton and do not react with Na2CO3. It fails the acidity test.
options.D: 2-bromobutanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(Br)CO}_2\text{H}$, has a carboxylic acid group so it reacts with Na2CO3 to release CO2. Its C-2 is attached to H, Br, $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, four different groups, so it is chiral. It passes both tests.
